summary: Hirananda Sastri was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College, Oriental College, and Panjab University. He held posts at DAV College, the Archaeological Survey of India, and served as Director of Archaeology for Baroda State (1934–1942).
Hiroaki Yokoyama is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2013), where he also served as a research student (研究生).

Hirofumi Isoda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1963–1966), where he served as lecturer (~1968–1974) and associate professor (~1974–2002). He was attested as professor emeritus at Shimane University in 1974.

Hirofumi Toda was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Seiren Matsunami, served as a professor at Tokushima University (~1976–2000), and was a special researcher at Rissho University (attested 1985).
Hiroko Kawanami is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied under John Okell and Anna Allott. She served as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University (attested 2013–2016).
Hiroko Matsuoka works in Indology and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and held a post at Leipzig University (attested 2016).

Hiromasa Tosaki is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyushu University (PhD ~1959–1966) and Harvard (~1967–1969) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held posts at Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College and Kyushu University (professor ~1978–1994).
Hiromi Habata is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Freiburg and was a researcher at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich around 2007.
Hiromi Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Ryukoku University, where he served as a full-time lecturer (attested 1987) and was also affiliated in 2006.
Hiromu Kitanishi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Otani University (~1944–1948) and later served there as a professor from circa 1967 to 1991.
Hironori Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued PhD studies at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020), where he also held a post.

Hiroo Kashiwagi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963). He served as a professor at Matsusaka University (~1982–1999) and president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College (~1993–1999).
Hiroshi Aoyagi works in Japanology. He studied at International Christian University (~1976–1980) and held a post at Nanzan University around 2000.

Hiroshi Araki is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Kyoto University, and held posts at Aichi Prefectural University, Osaka University, and the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (professor since ~2010).

Hiroshi Kanno is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1982). He served as Director at Soka University (~1988–2022) and Director of the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~1996–2009).

Hiroshi Marui is an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Savitribai Phule Pune University. He studied under Albrecht Wezler and held academic posts at Musashino University, University of Hamburg, and the University of Tokyo.
Hiroshi Maruyama is a scholar in Indology. He held a post as professor at Osaka University and headed the Ayurveda Kenkyūkai (both attested 1987).
Hiroshi Nemoto is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed an MA at Hiroshima University, where he also served as professor (attested 2015).
Hiroshi Yamashita is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Madras and served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).
Hirotomo Teranishi served as director at Soka University (attested 2010–2011), having succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009.
